originalTitle: FPIs emerge as biggest sellers among anchor investors in IPOs' 30-day window: Sebi study
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news item: A study by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) found that foreign investors were the biggest sellers of stocks among a group called anchor investors, who buy stocks when a company first lists on the market. These anchor investors were selling their stocks heavily around 30 days after the company's initial public offering (IPO), which put pressure on the stock price. This selling was more intense for smaller IPOs, meaning the stock prices of smaller companies were more affected. This is notable because anchor investors are expected to hold onto their stocks for a certain period, but the study found that they were selling them much sooner. This selling pattern can impact the overall performance of the stocks in the market.

originalTitle: Bill Ackman adds Netflix, Visa & Mastercard in biggest portfolio shake-up in years
simplifiedContent: Investor Bill Ackman has made some big changes to the companies he invests in. He has added Netflix, Visa, and Mastercard to his portfolio, which means he now owns a part of these companies. He has also invested in a few other companies, including Alcon, Intercontinental Exchange, and S&P Global. This is a significant update to his investments, and it's one of the biggest changes he's made in years. By adding these well-known companies, Ackman is shifting the makeup of his investment portfolio, which could impact his overall investment strategy.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
simplifiedContent: Here's what happened in the stock market: the Sensex, which is a measure of the market's performance, went up by 114 points, but the Nifty, another important measure, actually went down by over 40 points. This happened on a day when contracts were set to expire, which can cause unusual market movements. The fact that inflation, or the rate at which prices are rising, was lower than expected helped investors feel a bit better, but they were still worried about high oil prices and global tensions. As a result, the Nifty didn't move much and stayed within a certain range, which means it didn't go up or down too much. This mixed movement shows that investors are being cautious and waiting to see what happens next.

originalTitle: Sebi proposes colour-coded risk meter for bonds
simplifiedContent: The stock market regulator, Sebi, has a new idea to help investors like you make better decisions. They want to use a color-coded system to show how risky a bond is, so it's easier to understand. This system would take the complicated credit ratings and turn them into six simple color codes, making it easier for you to assess debt securities. This matters because it could help you avoid investing in bonds that are too risky for your comfort level. By doing this, Sebi aims to make investing in bonds more straightforward and accessible for individual investors.

originalTitle: FPIs lead the exit as anchor investors after IPO lock-ins end: Sebi study
simplifiedContent: A recent study by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) looked at what happens to stocks after they are first sold to the public (called an IPO). The study found that big investors, called anchor investors, tend to sell their shares slowly after they are allowed to do so. Foreign investors (FPIs) sell their shares much faster than other types of investors, like mutual funds. This selling can cause the stock price to drop, especially if the IPO was small or if a lot of shares were sold at once. The study analyzed 242 different IPOs to come to these conclusions.

originalTitle: Multibagger Mercury EV-Tech stock to be in focus on Friday after June quarter results
simplifiedContent: Mercury EV-Tech, a company that invests in electric vehicle technology, recently shared its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year 2027. The company's revenue, or the amount of money it made, increased by 47.9% compared to the same time last year, which is a positive sign. However, its net profit, or the amount of money it made after expenses, actually decreased by 4.2% due to rising costs. The company's stock price has also dropped significantly, by 74%, from its high point in 2024. This news may affect the stock's price on Friday, making it a day to watch for investors who own or are interested in Mercury EV-Tech stock.
